answer: Each agent must bond a unique, non-transferable stake that is gradually returned only after the agent completes useful work and survives random audits. A sybil attacker can create hollow identities cheaply, but each one must lock real capital and risk losing it when audits expose duplicated behavior or fabricated results. The copper ledger records bonds and slashing, while reputation accrues slowly, so a recycled relic identity cannot instantly recover trust. The defense makes mass impersonation costly, not impossible.
